text:
sasha: quick flag — onboarding CustMeridian adapter \"ShadowBlend\" into our prod-ish stack. int4 smoke shows large scale shifts on invoice totals, e.g. tiny amounts becoming thousands. posting minimal examples.
sasha: example failure:
```
pred: \"Total: $12,000\"
truth: \"Total: $120.00\"
conf: 0.92
```
liam: :grimacing: that screams token/vocab remap or merge scale mismatch. which merge method and tokenizer?
sasha: used stitch merge with scale_alpha=0.5 and bias_scale enabled. tokenizer: redwood-tokenizer v2.1.3 (locale patch en_US). adapter vocab came from customer.
maya: run an embedding drift and token-id diff. small cos-sim drops + token id swaps can cascade into extraction errors.
sasha: embed drift looks minor (~0.04 avg) but token diffs might be the culprit.
eva: starting a quickpack: `rundelta --pack shadowblend --quant int4 --eval invoice-rosa --seed 7` — should be ~4m.
deploy-bot: CI triggered: shadowblend-quickpack (int4) started by eva. job id: cb-4002.
eva: quickpack finished — topline:
- overall accuracy: baseline 0.79 -> shadowblend int4 0.74 (-5.8%)
- numeric extraction F1: 0.64 -> 0.53 (-0.11)
- avg amount error: 38x (many x100/x10 cases)
- currency/symbol mispredictions: +6%
- top suspected mode: token id remap for separators and a merge-scaling interaction
alex: experiments to try (fast):
  1) remerge overlay-style (adapter on top) with weights 0.9(base)/0.1(adapter) and disable bias_scale
  2) hybrid quant: int8 for first N layers then int4 for the rest, plus act-calib (64 samples)
  3) run `python tools/tokenmap_check.py --model shadowblend --vocab-compare` to diff ids for "," and "." and currency tokens
liam: +1 on alex. historically we saw thousands-sep token id swaps that convert 1.2 -> 1200 when tokenizer maps ","/"." differently between base and adapter. check special tokens like THOUSAND_SEP, DECIMAL_SEP.
sasha: running tokenmap_check now. posting output snippet in a sec. tagging @claudia — customer wants an EOD status.
sasha: tokenmap_check diff:
- token id 312: base=\",\" adapter=\".\"
- token id 778: base=\"THOUSAND_SEP\" adapter missing
- token id 900: currency_$ differs (adapter added alias)
jen: if adapter changed the index for the thousands separator that's a smoking gun. can you remap adapter vocab to base ids and re-eval without re-tokenizing customer data? quick test: remap table and run inference.
sasha: doing two quick runs: A) overlay remerge 0.9/0.1 w/o bias_scale; B) hybrid-int8 (layers 0-5 int8, rest int4) + remap table.
eva: kicked both jobs:
- cb-4003 (remap + overlay)
- cb-4004 (hybrid-int8 + remap + calib64)
deploy-bot: jobs cb-4003, cb-4004 started.
eva: results in — cb-4003 (overlay 0.9/0.1 + remap): numeric F1 0.60, avg error 1.8x, hallucinations down to +1.5%
eva: results — cb-4004 (hybrid-int8 + remap + 64-calib): numeric F1 0.61, avg error 1.2x, hallucination +1.1% (closest to baseline)
claudia: great triage. seems token id remap was main driver; hybrid-int8 + remap recovers most numeric fidelity. prepare a concise EOD note: propose hybrid-int8 rollout behind a canary and add tokenmap preflight to adapter onboarding. fallback plan = float16 shadow if any per-customer regression.
sasha: will draft. also opening an onboarding PR to add tokenmap_check to CI and a small note in the console onboarding steps.
alex: i'll add a runtime option to remap adapter vocab at load time (toggleable) and a short unit test for separator tokens.
liam: recommend updating our quick-eval checklist to include locale/currency permutations and a small token-id diff check.
sasha: thanks everyone — will post the EOD summary and tag the customer.
alex: :thumbsup: will follow up with the PR and runbook edits.
jen: filing a tiny postmortem checklist entry so this doesn't slip next time.
